claims.statement: The desktop executable becomes a headless MCP stdio server when started with --mcp-stdio: that mode opens no window, reads no project store and performs no client registration, and only forwards tool calls to a running desktop over the local socket.

The MCP bridge endpoint is derived from the Electron userData path by hashing it to a short digest and placing a socket under the OS temp directory on Unix or a named pipe on Windows, so different user profiles or checkouts do not share one endpoint.

On Unix the bridge unlinks a stale endpoint before listening and narrows the socket to 0600 after listen succeeds, while named pipes skip both steps; each connection carries one newline-delimited JSON request and response, capped at 64 MiB and correlated by a caller-supplied id.

The MCP server exposes fourteen tools from TOOL_NAMES — ten reads plus four writes (apply_model_patch and the three fulfillment operators) — while a stale doc comment above createEvidenceTools and the package README table still describe seven; only the four writers are annotated readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint true and idempotentHint false, and every tool declares openWorldHint false.

apply_model_patch is the only write path: the three operator tools first read the current document with get_domain_model, build their commands against it, and then submit those commands through the same applyModelPatch call, so operator patches and hand-written batches share guards and undo history.

The desktop main process routes get_app_state, get_domain_model, get_selected_entity, apply_model_patch and the get_capture_rect geometry call to the renderer holding the live ModelSession, while key data audit and stage gate are answered from a per-project cached sensors engine, delivery topology and the OpenAPI export come from the delivery service, replay and drift audit come from the simulation service, and the screenshot uses WebContents capture of a renderer-measured rect.

The renderer applies an external patch by decoding the wire commands and calling session.dispatchAll once with the label mcp-patch, so the whole patch is one undo step; post-dispatch validation issues are returned as blocking diagnostics but do not roll the patch back.

Renderer-bound bridge calls are correlated by a per-call UUID and bounded by a 15 second desktop timeout and a 10 second stdio-client timeout; the screenshot path hides editor chrome around capturePage and encodes PNG to keep thin diagram lines legible.
The MCP sensor service reports producedBy 'unavailable' instead of an empty ledger when the model cannot be read, and reports a gate that cannot execute as passed false with exit code 1.

Client registration merges an evidence-desktop entry (the same executable with --mcp-stdio and EVIDENCE_MCP_ENDPOINT) into Cursor and, on macOS and Windows, Claude Desktop configs, but only when the client's own directory already exists, and it preserves unrelated servers and keys.
A stdio MCP client that cannot reach the desktop returns an offline app state with isRunning false only for get_app_state; every other method surfaces the bridge error instead of an empty result.
The MCP bridge tests assert a real Unix socket round trip, the 0600 socket mode, a timeout code of RENDERER_UNAVAILABLE, and endpoint reuse after close.

The intended call order ships as SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS, which createEvidenceMcpServer passes to the McpServer constructor as instructions rather than leaving it in individual tool descriptions: read get_app_state first, prefer the three operators, otherwise use apply_model_patch, never write .evidence/fm files, check get_key_data_audit and run_stage_gate after a patch, and use the delivery, replay and drift reads for what the model becomes or whether it still holds.

The MCP surface is transport-free: createEvidenceTools returns plain tool objects that can be tested without a transport, and createEvidenceMcpServer is the only binding to the MCP SDK, registering each tool and converting thrown failures and PNG attachments into CallToolResult content.

Every main-process answer — sensors, delivery topology, OpenAPI export, scenario replay and drift audit — first asks the renderer for get_app_state to resolve the active project root, so all of them require an open editor window and raise NO_ACTIVE_PROJECT before touching the filesystem when no project is loaded.

The two delivery reads project the saved FM sources through the same readDelivery the delivery hub uses and return the bundle's limitations alongside the service topology or the OpenAPI document with a path count, so an external agent plans against what would be handed off rather than unsaved canvas edits, and neither tool writes a contract.

The two simulation reads work on the saved model: replay runs replayValidationSuite over the loaded sources and returns summaries for every scenario but per-frame detail only for the scenario that was named, folds source issues, suite errors and a no-scenarios note into errors, and both replay and drift answer passed false with the read error instead of throwing when the model directory is unreadable.

In --mcp-stdio mode the bridge endpoint is taken from EVIDENCE_MCP_ENDPOINT when the variable is set and is only re-derived from the Electron userData path otherwise, which lets a hand-written client config target a running desktop app without recomputing the digest.

get_app_state's mcp block is filled by the renderer with placeholder counters (connections 1, calls 0), so it is informational only; the real connection and served-call counts live in the McpStatus the main process publishes and pushes to every window.

A failure that is not an EvidenceMcpError is normalized to INTERNAL_ERROR when it crosses the socket, so a missing editor window surfaces as INTERNAL_ERROR rather than RENDERER_UNAVAILABLE, and because the stdio client's 10 s timeout is shorter than the desktop's 15 s renderer timeout a hung renderer is reported by the client first.
